findings.claim: The plan stores the session id in the handoff's front matter as its key. That is an extension field, and manifesto invariant I4 (backed by ADR 0006) says kmctl uses only OKF v0.2 fields and adds no extension fields yet. The plan does not name the field or say how it squares with I4. As written, building it breaks an accepted invariant without a decision. The spec and the pinned okf_validate.py 0.10.1 accept unknown keys (its comment cites spec section 11), so validation is fine; the conflict is with kmctl's own contract. To revise, either record an ADR that amends I4 for this one field (and name the field), or keep the key out of a new field.

The update path is what makes a second /handoff in one session replace the same handoff, and the Done-when line never tests it. It covers only the ordering and expiry of `kmctl handoffs` and the skill prompts. The plan never says that `kmctl new handoff --key` with an existing key replaces the body and description, keeps the file name and index entry (no second index entry, even if the title changes), logs one update line, and creates a new handoff for an unknown key. The eval has no rows. A build could pass Done-when while still adding a duplicate handoff, which defeats the reason for the spike. Add these to the Done-when line and the eval.
ADR 0009 names handoff_key as kmctl's one extension field, and manifesto I4 now allows extension fields an ADR names. The plan names the field and cites the ADR. The conflict with I4 is settled.

Done-when now tests the update path: an existing key replaces body and description, keeps the file name and index entry, writes one log line; an unknown key creates a new handoff; strict okf validation afterwards.

kmctl accepts an empty or blank --key, stores handoff_key "" and then matches every other empty-keyed handoff, so a second session with no id overwrites the first session's handoff. The /handoff SKILL.md code block passes --key "$CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID" unconditionally, so running it as written with the variable unset leads to exactly this.

The repeat-update dedup compares against the last line of log.md regardless of date, so an update on a later day whose previous log line is the same update logs nothing, with no heading for that day. It also departs from row r1 and the plan, which say every keyed update appends one log line.

The continue skill-creator runs never exercised the AskUserQuestion multi-select or step 3 (load and summarize the chosen handoffs). The one pick run used the fallback and listed four handoffs with no more option, which fails evals.json expectation 2 for that prompt, and results.md does not report that expectation. Row r6 asks that the results show no failed prompt.

The update path skips the title check that create applies, so kmctl new handoff '!!!' --key K rewrites an existing handoff with title "!!!" and heading "# !!!", while the same title is refused on create.
